newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Interest rate cut inspires surge in Manila shares.
newsitem.headline: Interest rate cut inspires surge in Manila shares.

text.p: Philippine shares won back a little of their sparkle on Thursday largely because of a cut in overnight rates but analysts said gains will be short-lived unless the currency market stabilises.

"While people cheered the rate reduction, many of them are still keeping a cautious eye on the currency since the earlier attack on the peso is not just a local problem. Foreign buying is still in trickles," said a foreign broker.

"What we are waiting for is stability. The market is acting as erratic as the forex and interest rates. Bargain-hunters may be able to drive up stocks in this kind of market but the sober minds would probably wait," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities.
The main index snapped out of two days of heavy losses on Thursday, closing up 33.02 points, or 1.28 percent, at 2,620.38 points.
On Thursday, the Central Bank lowered overnight borrowing rates by four percentage points to 28 percent from 32 percent.
The Bank earlier raised interest rates to defend the peso prior to its decision last Friday to effectively devalue the currency.
Analysts said the high interest rates spooked equities investors, driving them to higher yielding fixed-income instruments.

"Interest rates are being adjusted downwards albeit very slowly. That's a very good signal. The wild swings have been contained and there's not much bad news," said Helen Alvarez, research director at All Asia Securities.
But while the market barometer soared, in the broad market, gainers and losers numbered the same at 62 with 54 issues unchanged.

"This means that everyone is still cautious on what to do, on whether to enter at this time when there is no definite direction yet of the peso-dollar rate," said Carl Valentin, analyst at Asia Pacific Capital Equities.
"Despite the gains, we can't expect too many miracles. We are still in a soul-searching mood," Manuel Goseco, analyst at Dharmala Securities said.
Anscor-Hagedorn Securities analyst Cecilio Angelo Castro believes foreign exchange fears will continue to hang over the equities market for several weeks.
In the near-term, the market may be bolstered by the Central Bank's announcement of possibly another interest rate cut.

"It will be favourable for the market. We have always said that most of the listed issues will not benefit from a depreciation of the peso. With another cut, the situation will not be as bad before," said Spencer Yap, analyst at BPI Securities Corp.
Traders have pegged resistance at 2,700 points.
